Deprecated SDK imports removed¶

This project no longer depends on bigdata-client or bigdata-research-tools. See MIGRATION_NOTES.md / README.md and Thematic_Screener_CLI for the REST + bigdata-smart-batching + OpenAI pattern. Pass company CSVs (RP_ENTITY_ID, COMPANY_NAME) instead of watchlists.

AI Disruption Risk Report Generator¶

Automated Analysis of AI Threats and Opportunities in Technology Companies¶

Why It Matters¶

AI disruption requires identifying which companies will thrive versus those vulnerable to displacement, but evaluating AI positioning across scattered news, earnings calls, and filings is resource-intensive. Investment decisions need systematic analysis of both AI risks and strategic responses to identify winners and potential shorts.

What It Does¶

The GenerateReport class in the bigdata-research-tools package systematically evaluates both AI disruption risks and proactive AI adoption across company watchlists using unstructured data from multiple sources. Built for portfolio managers and financial analysts, it transforms scattered AI-related information into quantifiable positioning intelligence and identifies investment opportunities based on AI readiness.

How It Works¶

The Report Generator combines semantic content retrieval, dual-theme analysis, and comparative scoring methodologies to deliver:

  • Risk-proactivity assessment measuring both AI disruption vulnerability and strategic AI adoption initiatives
  • Standardized scoring system enabling cross-company comparison of AI positioning and competitive readiness
  • Investment intelligence generation revealing underlying narratives that shape each company's AI transformation journey
  • Structured output for reporting ranking companies by AI resilience and strategic positioning

A Real-World Use Case¶

This cookbook demonstrates the complete workflow through analyzing AI disruption risks and proactive responses across a company watchlist, showing how the generator automatically quantifies AI positioning and identifies potential investment opportunities based on strategic AI readiness.

Setup and Imports¶

Async Compatibility Setup¶

Run this cell first - Required for Google Colab, Jupyter Notebooks, and VS Code with Jupyter extension:

Why is this needed?¶

Interactive environments (Colab, Jupyter) already have an asyncio event loop running. When bigdata-research-tools makes async API calls (like to OpenAI), you'll get this error without nest_asyncio:

RuntimeError: asyncio.run() cannot be called from a running event loop

The nest_asyncio.apply() command patches this to allow nested event loops.

💡 Tip: If you're unsure which environment you're in, just run the cell below - it won't hurt in any environment!

In [1]:
import datetime
start = datetime.datetime.now()
In [2]:
try:
    import asyncio
    asyncio.get_running_loop()
    import nest_asyncio; nest_asyncio.apply()
    print("✅ nest_asyncio applied")
except (RuntimeError, ImportError):
    print("✅ nest_asyncio not needed or not available")

✅ nest_asyncio applied

Defining the Report Parameters¶

Fixed Parameters¶

  • Keywords (keywords): Keywords used for improving retrieval
  • Main Theme (main_theme_risk): The central concept to explore
  • Main Theme Proactivity (main_theme_proactivity): Proactive measures and strategies companies take to address the main theme risk
  • List of sentences about risk themes (list_sentences_risks): Sentences used to improve the retrieval regarding the main theme
  • List of sentences about risk proactivity themes (list_sentences_proactivity): Sentences used to improve the retrieval regarding the proactivity against the main theme
  • Bigdata (bigdata): Bigdata connection

Customizable Parameters¶

  • Watchlist (my_watchlist_id): The set of companies to analyze. This is the ID of your watchlist in https://app.bigdata.com/watchlists

  • Model Selection (llm_model): The LLM model used to label search result document chunks and generate summaries

  • Frequency (freq): The frequency of the date ranges to search over. Supported values:

    • Y: Yearly intervals.
    • M: Monthly intervals.
    • W: Weekly intervals.
    • D: Daily intervals. Defaults to M.

  • Time Period (start_date and end_date): The date range over which to run the analysis

  • Fiscal Year (fiscal_year): If the document type is transcripts or filings, fiscal year needs to be specified

  • Focus (focus): Specify a focus within the main theme

  • Document Limit (document_limit_news, document_limit_filings, document_limit_transcripts): The maximum number of documents to return per query to Bigdata API for each category of documents

  • Batch Size (batch_size): The number of entities to include in a single batched query

In [8]:
# ===== Fixed Parameters =====

# Keywords for filtering content
keywords = ['AI']

# Risk Theme
main_theme_risk = 'Risks or concerns related to AI disruption'

# Proactivity Theme
main_theme_proactivity = 'Integrating GenAI into products or forming partnerships to improve GenAI offerings'

# Sentences expressing risk-related narratives
list_sentences_risks = [
    "Companies face substantial risks from AI-driven market disruptions today.",
    "AI advancements threaten traditional business models and competitive advantages.",
    "Disruption by AI can lead to loss of market share rapidly.",
    "Existing workflows may become obsolete due to AI innovations.",
    "Companies risk being outpaced by agile AI-focused competitors."
]

# Sentences expressing proactivity-related narratives
list_sentences_proactivity = [
    "Companies actively incorporate GenAI to enhance product offerings and features.",
    "Partnerships aim to improve GenAI solutions in competitive markets.",
    "Proactive firms leverage GenAI technology to boost customer engagement strategies.",
    "Organizations collaborate to advance GenAI capabilities and applications effectively.",
    "Firms invest in GenAI partnerships to innovate their service delivery."
]
In [9]:
# ===== Customizable Parameters =====

# Company Universe (CSV with RP_ENTITY_ID + COMPANY_NAME, instead of a platform watchlist)
universe_path = "../Thematic_Screener_CLI/40_companies.csv"
universe_df = load_universe(universe_path).reset_index(drop=True)
companies = [SimpleNamespace(id=row.RP_ENTITY_ID, name=row.COMPANY_NAME) for row in universe_df.itertuples()]
company_names = [c.name for c in companies]
print(f"Universe: {len(universe_df)} companies -> {company_names}")

# LLM Specification
llm_model = "gpt-5.6-luna"

# Search Frequency (kept for compatibility; not used by smart-batching search)
search_frequency = 'M'

# Specify Time Range (narrow window for cost control)
start_date = "2025-01-01"
end_date = "2025-04-20"

# Fiscal Year
fiscal_year = 2025

# Document Limits (scope gates: >0 enables that document scope's search)
document_limit_news = 10
document_limit_filings = 5
document_limit_transcripts = 5

# Others
batch_size = 1
chunk_percentage = 0.05  # cost control: sample a small percentage of matching chunks per query
max_rows_to_label = 10_000

Generate Report¶

We’re now initializing the GenerateReport class, and in the next section of the cookbook, we’ll walk through each step it takes to build the report.

But hey, if you'd rather skip the step-by-step and jump straight to the result, just run the cell below and then click here and you are good to go!🚀 Just remember follow the brief instructions to run generate_report() !

In [10]:
report_generator = GenerateReport(
        universe_df=universe_df,
        keywords=keywords,
        main_theme_risk=main_theme_risk,
        main_theme_proactivity=main_theme_proactivity,
        list_sentences_risks=list_sentences_risks,
        list_sentences_proactivity=list_sentences_proactivity,
        llm_model=llm_model,
        api_key=OPENAI_API_KEY,
        start_date=start_date,
        end_date=end_date,
        fiscal_year=fiscal_year,
        search_frequency=search_frequency,
        document_limit_news=document_limit_news,
        document_limit_filings=document_limit_filings,
        document_limit_transcripts=document_limit_transcripts,
        batch_size=batch_size,
        chunk_percentage=chunk_percentage,
)

Workflow step by step¶

Retrieve Content¶

You can leverage the Bigdata API to run a search on company news, filings and transcripts.

In [11]:
# Retrieve content per document scope via bigdata-smart-batching (REST), through the
# GenerateReport.retrieve_documents() helper (uses report_generator's configured
# universe / date-range / sentences; document_limit_* act as scope on/off gates).
df_risk_list = []
df_proactivity_list = []

doc_configs = [
    ("news", document_limit_news),
    ("filings", document_limit_filings),
    ("transcripts", document_limit_transcripts),
]

for doc_scope, doc_limit in doc_configs:
    if doc_limit > 0:
        df_risk_scope, df_proactivity_scope = report_generator.retrieve_documents(
            doc_scope=doc_scope,
            doc_limit=doc_limit,
            doc_type_name=doc_scope,
            fiscal_year=fiscal_year,
        )
        df_risk_list.append(df_risk_scope)
        df_proactivity_list.append(df_proactivity_scope)

# Combine all risk dataframes into a single dataset
df_sentences_semantic_risk = pd.concat(df_risk_list, ignore_index=True)

# Combine all proactivity dataframes into a single dataset
df_sentences_semantic_proactivity = pd.concat(df_proactivity_list, ignore_index=True)

# Cost control: cap the number of rows sent downstream to OpenAI for labeling/summarization
df_sentences_semantic_risk = df_sentences_semantic_risk.head(max_rows_to_label).reset_index(drop=True) if len(df_sentences_semantic_risk) > max_rows_to_label else df_sentences_semantic_risk
df_sentences_semantic_proactivity = df_sentences_semantic_proactivity.head(max_rows_to_label).reset_index(drop=True) if len(df_sentences_semantic_proactivity) > max_rows_to_label else df_sentences_semantic_proactivity

print(f"Risk chunks retrieved (capped): {len(df_sentences_semantic_risk)}")
print(f"Proactivity chunks retrieved (capped): {len(df_sentences_semantic_proactivity)}")

Label the Results¶

Use an LLM to analyze each document chunk and determine its relevance to the main theme. Any document chunks which aren't explicitly linked to AI Disruption Risk will be filtered out.

In [14]:
labeler = SimpleLabeler(model=llm_model, api_key=OPENAI_API_KEY)

df_risk_labels = labeler.get_labels(
                main_theme=main_theme_risk,
                labels=['risk'],
                texts=df_sentences_semantic_risk["masked_text"].tolist()
            )

# Merge the datasets
df_risk_labeled = pd.merge(df_sentences_semantic_risk, df_risk_labels, left_index=True, right_index=True)

df_proactivity_labels = labeler.get_labels(
                main_theme=main_theme_proactivity,
                labels=['proactivity'],
                texts=df_sentences_semantic_proactivity["masked_text"].tolist()
            )

# Merge the datasets
df_proactivity_labeled = pd.merge(df_sentences_semantic_proactivity, df_proactivity_labels, left_index=True, right_index=True)


# Process the results
df_risk_labeled_relevant = df_risk_labeled.loc[~df_risk_labeled.label.isin(['', 'unassigned', 'unclear'])].copy()
df_proactivity_labeled_relevant = df_proactivity_labeled.loc[~df_proactivity_labeled.label.isin(['', 'unassigned', 'unclear'])].copy()

Document Distribution Visualization¶

You can visualize the tables showing the count of different document types for each company in the given universe. This helps you understand the distribution and availability of information across different sources for each entity.

In [15]:
create_styled_table(df_risk_labeled_relevant, title='Relevant Document Count for AI Disruption Risk by Company and Document Type', companies_list = company_names)
In [16]:
create_styled_table(df_proactivity_labeled_relevant, title='Relevant Document Count for AI Proactivity by Company and Document Type', companies_list = company_names)

Summarizer¶

The following code is used to create a summary for each company using the information from the retrieved documents.

In [17]:
summarizer_company = SummarizerCompany(
    model=llm_model,
    api_key=OPENAI_API_KEY,
    logger= GenerateReport.logger,
    verbose=True
)
In [18]:
df_risk_by_company = asyncio.run(
            summarizer_company.process_by_company(
                df_labeled=df_risk_labeled_relevant,
                list_entities=companies,
                theme=main_theme_risk,
                focus='risk'
            ))

df_proactivity_by_company = asyncio.run(
            summarizer_company.process_by_company(
                df_labeled=df_proactivity_labeled_relevant,
                list_entities=companies,
                theme=main_theme_proactivity,
                focus=''
            )
        )

Getting the Scores¶

Processing the datasets and computing the AI Disruption Risk Score and AI Proactivity Score.

In [19]:
dfr = df_risk_by_company[['entity_id', 'entity_name', 'topic_summary', 'n_documents']].copy()
dfr = dfr.rename(columns={'topic_summary': 'risk_summary', 'n_documents': 'n_documents_risk'})
dfp = df_proactivity_by_company[['entity_id', 'entity_name', 'topic_summary', 'n_documents']].copy()
dfp = dfp.rename(columns={'topic_summary': 'proactivity_summary', 'n_documents': 'n_documents_proactivity'})
df_by_company = dfr.merge(dfp, on=['entity_id', 'entity_name'], how='outer')

df_by_company['n_documents_risk'] = df_by_company['n_documents_risk'].fillna(0)
df_by_company['n_documents_proactivity'] = df_by_company['n_documents_proactivity'].fillna(0)
df_by_company['ai_disruption_risk_score'] = df_by_company['n_documents_risk']/df_by_company['n_documents_risk'].mean()
df_by_company['ai_proactivity_score'] = df_by_company['n_documents_proactivity']/df_by_company['n_documents_proactivity'].mean()
df_by_company['ai_proactivity_minus_disruption_risk_score'] = df_by_company['ai_proactivity_score'] - df_by_company['ai_disruption_risk_score']

Final Dataset¶

The final dataset for the report is generated by processing and merging the risk and proactivity datasets.

In [20]:
df_quotes_risk = GenerateReport.aggregate_verbatim(df_risk_labeled_relevant, 'risk')
df_by_company = pd.merge(df_by_company, df_quotes_risk, how='left', on='entity_name')
df_quotes_proactivity = GenerateReport.aggregate_verbatim(df_proactivity_labeled_relevant, 'proactivity')
df_report = pd.merge(df_by_company, df_quotes_proactivity, how='left', on='entity_name')

Direct method¶

Once the class GenerateReport is initialized you can just run the method generate_report() to get the final output and then you can run the functions to visualize the results and to generate the report.

For practical reasons you can also choose to import and/or export the intermediate outputs to/from a specific directory:

  • import_from_path: File path from where the intermediate outputs will be loaded
  • export_to_path: File path where the intermediate outputs will be saved

To run the direct method uncomment the variable DIRECT_METHOD

To export the intermediate results / final outputs uncomment the variable EXPORT_RESULTS

In [22]:
# Uncomment the flag DIRECT_METHOD to run the workflow
#DIRECT_METHOD_FLAG = True
#EXPORT_RESULTS_FLAG = True

if 'DIRECT_METHOD_FLAG' in globals() and DIRECT_METHOD_FLAG:
  if 'EXPORT_RESULTS_FLAG' in globals() and EXPORT_RESULTS_FLAG:
    report = report_generator.generate_report(import_from_path=output_dir, export_to_path=output_dir)
  else:
    report = report_generator.generate_report()
  df_report = report.report_by_company
  df_report.head(5)

Generate Final Report¶

The final report will be saved as a html file in the folder export_path

In [25]:
display_report(df_report=df_report, score='ai_proactivity_minus_disruption_risk_score', top='top', nb_entities=5, export_to_path=output_dir+'/report_ai_disruption_top_5.html')
AI Disruption Risk and Proactive Responses

AI Disruption Risk and Proactive Responses

August 27, 2026

Score Definitions

AI Disruption Risk Score: The number of unique documents related to the risk of GenAI disruption, normalized by the average number of risk documents retrieved across the entire watchlist.

AI Proactivity Score: The number of unique documents related to the proactive adoption of GenAI, normalized by the average number of proactivity documents retrieved across the entire watchlist.

AI Proactivity Minus Disruption Risk Score: The difference between the AI Proactivity Score and the AI Disruption Risk Score. A higher score indicates a stronger company response relative to the identified risks.

Top 5 Companies for AI Proactivity Minus Disruption Risk Score

Alphabet Inc.

AI Proactivity Minus Disruption Risk Score: 3.82

AI Disruption Risk Score: 4.88 / Nb Documents Risk: 114.0

AI Proactivity Score: 8.70 / Nb Documents Proactivity: 126.0

AI Disruption Risk

AI-powered alternatives such as ChatGPT Search, Anthropic, Perplexity and other conversational assistants could shift users away from Google Search, eroding Alphabet’s market share, advertising revenue and publisher ecosystem; Google Search and related services generate over half of Alphabet’s consolidated revenue, while AI Overviews have reportedly reduced organic position-one click-through rates from 50% to 28–30% and may cut organic traffic by 15–64%. Alphabet faces substantial monetization and capital-allocation risk from heavy AI investment: its 2025 capital-expenditure outlook was nearly 30% above consensus, investors question Gemini’s usage and revenue, and DeepSeek reportedly matched advanced Google-model capabilities at materially lower training cost after spending $5.6 million, increasing pressure for lower prices and raising doubts about billions in planned spending. Execution and reputational risks remain after Gemini’s inaccurate image generation in early 2024 was temporarily suspended and contributed to roughly $90 billion in lost Alphabet market value; AI-generated code also creates quality, stability and security concerns, despite Google reporting that about 25% of its codebase is AI-written. Google Cloud’s AI expansion carries exposure to intense competition, pricing pressure, regulatory compliance, cyberattacks, data leakage and risky configurations—Tenable found 77% of organizations using Vertex AI Workbench had at least one notebook with an overly privileged service account—while evolving AI, privacy, copyright and antitrust rules could require new investments, fines or structural restrictions.

AI Proactivity

Alphabet is expanding GenAI through Gemini, Vertex AI, Google Workspace, Google Customer Engagement Suite, and models such as Imagen and Veo; its 2024 Annual Report says Vertex AI enables developers to train, tune, augment, test, and deploy applications, while Gemini for Google Cloud provides pre-packaged agents for software development and cybersecurity. Google Cloud is deepening partnerships to embed these capabilities into products and industries, including ServiceNow integrations with BigQuery, Vertex AI and Google Workspace; Salesforce’s expanded partnership brings Gemini to Agentforce and integrates Service Cloud with Google’s customer-engagement tools; and collaborations with Accenture, Tech Mahindra, LTIMindtree, TCS, Capgemini, Kyndryl, Verizon, SAP, Lockheed Martin, Airtel, FlutterFlow and others support industry-specific deployment, modernization and agentic-AI offerings. Alphabet is also improving consumer and advertising products: an Associated Press real-time information feed will enhance the Gemini app, Project Astra and Chrome agent experiences can execute tasks such as recipe-based shopping, and YouTube’s GenAI tools for creators, viewers and advertisers include Veo, with GenAI-powered video campaigns delivering 17% higher return on ad spend than manual campaigns. Additional ecosystem activity includes the March 27, 2025 Kyndryl Gemini/mainframe-modernization program, Deutsche Telekom’s Gemini 2.0 and Vertex AI network agent, Persistent’s Pi-OmniKG healthcare collaboration, and Alphabet’s strategic AI and robotics collaboration with NVIDIA, broadening enterprise adoption and monetization opportunities for Google Cloud and GenAI products.

Microsoft Corp.

AI Proactivity Minus Disruption Risk Score: 2.83

AI Disruption Risk Score: 6.08 / Nb Documents Risk: 142.0

AI Proactivity Score: 8.91 / Nb Documents Proactivity: 129.0

AI Disruption Risk

Microsoft faces the risk that cheaper, efficient models such as China-based DeepSeek will commoditize AI, weaken the advantage of its OpenAI-linked offerings, and make its large infrastructure commitments uneconomic; DeepSeek-related concerns contributed to Microsoft share declines of about 4.5% and 3% on January 27, 2025, while the company reportedly shelved or deferred U.S. and European data-center projects representing up to 2 gigawatts. High AI spending may not translate into sufficient returns: Microsoft planned roughly $80 billion of fiscal-2025 AI infrastructure investment, yet investors cited slower Azure growth of about 21% and concerns that Copilot was costly, glitchy, and struggling to meet expectations, contributing to a reported potential $182 billion loss in market value. Rapid competition from AWS, Google Cloud, Salesforce, Oracle, smaller AI firms, and potentially OpenAI itself could pressure Azure, Copilot pricing, adoption, and market share, while reliance on OpenAI creates partnership and supply risks. Microsoft also identifies direct exposure to flawed or biased models, inaccurate, offensive, unlawful, or infringing outputs, data leakage, cyberattacks, privacy and copyright claims, EU AI Act and U.S. regulatory action, and resulting liability, reputational damage, or reduced customer acceptance; its January 29, 2025 Form 10-Q expressly warns these issues could impair products and business operations.

AI Proactivity

Microsoft is expanding GenAI adoption through Azure OpenAI Service, Microsoft 365 Copilot, GitHub Copilot, Microsoft Teams, Dynamics 365 AI and Azure AI, while relying on partners to build industry-specific solutions and extend its enterprise reach. Partnerships with Happiest Minds, Conduent, ASGN, HCLTech, NTT DATA, Sapiens, Amdocs, LTIMindtree, Fortanix, SymphonyAI, Pearson and others are integrating Microsoft technology into conversational assistants, contact centers, insurance platforms, secure custom applications, media solutions and workforce-skilling tools; ASGN’s February 2025 collaboration, for example, pilots Copilot for Microsoft 365 and Azure OpenAI Service, while Conduent launched a GenAI program with more than 20 use cases and a Microsoft innovation initiative. Customer deployments demonstrate measurable value for Microsoft’s offerings, including ABB’s Genix Copilot built with Azure OpenAI Service, which reportedly delivered up to 35% operations-and-maintenance savings, 20% better energy and emissions optimization and an 80% reduction in service calls, and Happiest Minds’ Azure-based Coca-Cola Beverages Vietnam solution, which improved HR and cooler-productivity workflows. Microsoft executives emphasized partner-led growth and responsible governance, with Nicole Dezen citing 5x ROI for every $1 invested in GenAI in India and higher margins for partners generating at least 25% of Microsoft-related revenue from AI, while integrations also create security demand as enterprises protect data used with Microsoft 365 Copilot.

Qualcomm Inc.

AI Proactivity Minus Disruption Risk Score: 0.88

AI Disruption Risk Score: 0.09 / Nb Documents Risk: 2.0

AI Proactivity Score: 0.97 / Nb Documents Proactivity: 14.0

AI Disruption Risk

Qualcomm faces increasing operational challenges in delivering seamless, end-to-end management of AI models and applications from enterprise cloud environments to edge devices such as mobile phones and cars, including concerns over AI outcomes, data use, and model lifecycle management. The proliferation of AI models and the difficulty of deploying compact, capable models at the edge could pressure Qualcomm to provide more flexible and responsible edge-AI capabilities. NVIDIA and AMD are aggressively expanding their AI-focused product offerings, creating a more competitive semiconductor landscape that could weigh on Qualcomm’s growth prospects. Evercore ISI and Cantor Fitzgerald rated Qualcomm Neutral in the week referenced, also citing valuation and margin-sustainability concerns amid competition.

AI Proactivity

Qualcomm is expanding on-device and enterprise GenAI capabilities across smartphones, PCs, cars and other products, with CEO Cristiano Amon describing AI as a major technology transition at SXSW and emphasizing devices that can process AI tasks locally. On April 1, 2025, Qualcomm acquired MovianAI, formerly VinAI’s generative-AI division, bringing in VinAI founder Hung Bui to strengthen GenAI R&D and accelerate solutions for smartphones, PCs and software-defined vehicles. Qualcomm also introduced its AI On-Prem Appliance and AI Inference Suite with first-wave partners including IBM and Honeywell, enabling privacy-sensitive GenAI and computer-vision inference on enterprise hardware, while its collaboration with EyePop.ai uses Qualcomm AI Hub to simplify Windows deployment of edge-optimized vision models. Partnerships with Cadence expanded Qualcomm’s EDA and systems-software support for next-generation AI designs, and collaboration with Zebra and Google applies GenAI agents and edge intelligence to retail frontline operations; Qualcomm is also investing in Vietnam-based R&D, partnerships and reference designs to support hybrid, privacy-preserving AI applications.

Booking Holdings Inc.

AI Proactivity Minus Disruption Risk Score: 0.52

AI Disruption Risk Score: 0.17 / Nb Documents Risk: 4.0

AI Proactivity Score: 0.69 / Nb Documents Proactivity: 10.0

AI Disruption Risk

At Booking Holdings’ Q4 2024 earnings call, management identified rising competition from agentic AI platforms that could bypass traditional booking channels and listings, potentially weakening Booking’s market position. New AI-driven technologies may alter the mix between paid and direct traffic, creating risks to profitability. Booking also noted that AI-related revenue benefits may take longer to materialize than cost savings, increasing uncertainty around the timing of returns from its AI investments.

AI Proactivity

Booking Holdings is integrating GenAI into its Connected Trip strategy through Booking.com’s AI Trip Planner, AI assistant/Penny, price-comparison tool, Smart Filter, Property Q&A, and experiments with AI-generated review summaries to make travel planning and customer service more personalized and frictionless. The company believes travel-specific AI agents—and collaboration among agents—can connect flights, accommodations, payments, and in-trip experiences, supporting a broader offering that included nearly 50 million airline tickets booked in 2024, up 38% year over year, with $13.1 billion in gross bookings. Booking is pursuing a dual approach of proprietary development and partnerships, including being named an OpenAI launch partner for Operator, working with leading generative-AI organizations, using OpenAI models to assist travelers, and supporting OpenTable’s use of Salesforce Agentforce; Agoda and KAYAK are also advancing GenAI within the group. Booking expects GenAI combined with its data and machine-learning capabilities to improve supplier partners’ businesses—particularly small and medium-sized businesses lacking access to sophisticated technology—and to help attract and satisfy travelers and partners.

Palantir Technologies Inc.

AI Proactivity Minus Disruption Risk Score: 0.23

AI Disruption Risk Score: 0.26 / Nb Documents Risk: 6.0

AI Proactivity Score: 0.48 / Nb Documents Proactivity: 7.0

AI Disruption Risk

Palantir faces increasing AI-driven competition from established enterprise software companies, specialized AI startups, and major cloud providers whose implementation, orchestration, and analytics tools increasingly overlap with its offerings. Further development of AI platforms by Microsoft, Google, and Amazon could weaken Palantir’s competitive edge, while lower-priced entrants such as DeepSeek may intensify price pressure and reduce profits across enterprise AI software. Its reliance on government contracts—particularly defense and intelligence—exposes the business to policy changes and defense-spending cuts, while controversy surrounding its government work may restrict commercial expansion in some markets. Palantir’s high valuation and stock volatility leave little room for execution errors or slower AI adoption, and rising enterprise fatigue over AI licensing and consumption costs could encourage FinOps-driven spending reductions.

AI Proactivity

Palantir’s strategic product partnership with Databricks integrates Unity Catalog and Delta Sharing with Palantir’s platform and military-grade security, lowering barriers to deploying governed, secure autonomous GenAI workflows; the joint offering is already supporting mission-critical work for the U.S. Department of Defense, Treasury, and Health and Human Services, bp, and other customers. Palantir is also expanding GenAI partnerships through KT, integrating its AI solutions with KT’s cloud and network infrastructure for optimized services in South Korea, and through TWG Global, whose April 2025 initiative aims to embed enterprise-wide AI across banking, investment management, and insurance. Its partnership with SAUR uses Palantir Foundry and AIP to apply generative AI to contract management, reducing processes to minutes and reaching more than 300 users within months. Palantir is additionally part of AIG’s technology-partner ecosystem, alongside Anthropic and AWS, supporting an agentic architecture after AIG deployed its first GenAI solution in 2024; L3Harris also cited its strategic Palantir partnership in developing integrated hardware, software, and AI capabilities.

Export the Results¶

            sheet_name="Report AI Disruption Risk",
            index=False,
            startrow=2,

        )
